concept.title: Where to buy components
concept.shortdesc: Components can be purchased either online or from physical retailers

conbody.p: Once you’ve finalized your parts list finding a good price from a seller with stock can be a challenging task. Prices can fluctuate over a matter of months depending on new technology, political circumstances, and changes in demand. Two parts that are near identical may vary significantly in price due to branding or seller.

The majority of sellers in the US operate through online storefronts rather than keeping stock in physical stores. While you might find a small local parts seller near you, there is only one brick and mortar retailer of note in the US: Micro Center.

section.p: The largest online computer parts suppliers in the US are Amazon and Newegg with Best Buy being a distant third, but their offerings and policies have become very similar over time. Newegg has a slightly more generous return policy with no restocking fees for returned goods, while Amazon inconsistently charges a percentage. In general, though, go with whichever merchant is listed on PCPartPicker’s parts list at the time to take advantage of sales.

Micro Center is the only nationwide brick and mortar computer parts retailer left in the US, but it has held on for a reason. Micro Center frequently has bundles and deals that nothing online can compare to, but such deals are almost always in store pick up only. Willingness and ability to travel to a Micro Center can result in significantly better parts for less than what would be available online or at any other retailer. Micro Center currently has 28 stores spread across the US in 19 states.
